lesson: [qwen3vl_8b] Digit-copy OV score predicted a real arithmetic part. Score = digit embedding mapped through a head's V/O onto the same digit's unembedding, diagonal minus off-diagonal. L23 heads 30/7/4 scored 5.7/5.2/4.7 vs under 1 for word/CJK/code tokens, and ablating [4,7,30,31] dropped two_digit_addition .414 (control -.002). Digit-copy heads in other layers did not matter, even much stronger ones: L29 at 55, L32 at 304, L33 at 111 all dropped it at most .02.

[qwen3vl_8b] Recipe for large MLP units: take the SVD subspace (top 12 dims) of the causal heads' OV outputs on digit tokens, then rank same-layer MLP units by the fraction of their gate+up row norm inside it. At L23 the 256/512/1024/2048-unit clusters all passed for addition (about .44 drop, random parts at most .02). The same recipe gave inert readers at L14, L22, L24 (own heads), L26, L29, L34 and L35. It only works where heads feed a computing MLP, not where heads write the answer directly.

[qwen3vl_8b] Digit-writer down_proj columns (contrastive cosine to the digit unembedding direction) were a real bottleneck at L34. The 64-1024 unit clusters dropped recall_first_number .47-.60 (word control near 0, random at most .005); the top units' logit lens is exactly the digits 0-9. The same recipe for month/colour/capital/CJK/accent/code writers was inert (at most .01). Those skills have about 11-nat margins vs 3.4 for digit recall, so check base margin first.

[qwen3vl_8b] Whole GQA groups (4 heads sharing v_proj) are a good head unit, and bisecting a layer's attention by groups finds them cheaply. All-L34 heads cut recall .433 but leaked into the control (-.151). Bisection found group 3 (heads 12-15) at .237 with control -.074, which passed. Bisection also isolated L35 group 6 (heads 24-27), which cuts math .21 together with recall .50.

[qwen3vl_8b] Attribution scans return at most 20 units per layer and missed the L23 heads entirely, so use them only for small seeds. Single-layer 20-unit sets were very clean: L22 list indexing passed at .211. Search-split results near .15-.18 failed held-out (L32 translation .176). Single blocks for facts or addition are risky: random blocks reached .78-.81 on those skills.

[qwen3vl_8b] Don't define overlapping agent skills such as addition and subtraction. Each becomes an 'other skill' for the other, which blocked screening the strongest arithmetic unit: L23 groups 1+7 dropped addition .643 and subtraction .56. The agent skill cap is 8, so plan skills before spending them.

[qwen3vl_8b] Seed growth from one dominant attribution unit made a real part. L22 MLP unit 5178 scored .071, against .013 for the next unit. Twelve more L22 seeds (attribution top 4629/10532/6365/6380 plus an earlier 20-unit set) went in with it, and units were added by summed gate/up/down weight cosine to the seeds. The 64-unit cluster passed python_list_index at .173 (other skills and controls ≤.015, random ≤.004). Stop at the size where the drop peaks: 96/128/256 units gave only .123/.10-.14/.126.

[qwen3vl_8b] The same seed growth from weak or flat seeds (attribution ≤.03) stayed under .10 at every size. Examples: en_fr at L32 gave .078/.093/.067 at 64/128/512, en_fr at L29/L31 .035/.003, list indexing at L23/L18/L34 .041/-.007/-.001, times_table at L10/L14 .035/0, multilingual at L33/L35 .077/.042. Check that one seed clearly dominates before spending screens on a cluster.

[qwen3vl_8b] Facts is spread across whole late layers, not a subset. The L31 block cut facts .47, while all 32 L31 heads gave only .012, so the effect is in the MLP. The top 6144 L31 MLP units by gate·up·down norm cut facts .234 cleanly, but random 6144-unit sets reached .15-.27 and the screen failed. The L28 block (.20) also lost to random blocks, one of which reached .47. Don't screen facts with blocks or half-layer MLP parts on this model.

[qwen3vl_8b] Attribution put almost all object_color head effect in L26 (heads 20/24/4/22/27/23). Ablating GQA groups 0,1,4,5,6 dropped colour .149 with everything else under .035, but random L26 parts reached .133 and the held-out check failed. A skill that random parts in the same layer can already drop about .13 can't pass, so test random parts before polishing.

[qwen3vl_8b] MLP columns aligned with the mean unembedding of a category's output tokens were inert at L28, at peak alignment (top-64 cosine .064-.070). The 256-unit sets for month, colour and code all dropped their skills ≤.007. The top times_table attribution unit at L35 (701, score .066) reads out as a '!'/'?' punctuation writer, not arithmetic. Read the logit lens of attribution seeds before growing them.

[qwen3vl_8b] Several head-group ablations were inert or hit the wrong skill. L35 groups 0-3 and 4,5,7 and L33 groups 0-3 had no effect on math or code. Multilingual heads at L20/L22 reached at most .078, and times_table heads at L14/L22/L23/L26 at most .038. Single blocks L25/L26 hit facts (.20/.23) and addition (.14/.13) together. Overlapping agent skills (addition, subtraction, times_table) used up the 8 skill slots and left no room to define new ones.

[qwen3vl_8b] The month version of the L34 digit-writer recipe was inert. L34/L35 down_proj columns ranked by cosine to the month unembedding, minus 0.5x the best other category, included strong single units (top cos .58/.64), yet the 256-unit clusters dropped month_successor ≤.003. Strong alignment of a late writer does not show that the skill depends on it, and month_successor seems carried upstream.

[qwen3vl_8b] The L23 addition heads are a shared number/sequence-successor unit, not an addition-only one. The 8 heads [4,7,20,25,28,29,30,31] dropped addition .463, subtraction .256 and month_successor .266 (control -.147). Adding GQA group 0 (12 heads) raised month to .318 (control -.131). To screen this as a broad arithmetic/sequence unit, define one combined skill instead of separate addition, subtraction and month skills.

[qwen3vl_8b] The L33 block hits facts .291, multilingual .205 and en_fr .138, but general_text drops .186 too, so it is not selective. All 32 L33 heads gave ≤.052, so the effect is in the MLP. The top 1024 L33 MLP units by gate·up·down norm dropped everything ≤.02, so the effect is spread across the layer, as with L31 for facts. Don't spend screens on norm-ranked late MLP subsets.

[qwen3vl_8b] The L20 block was nearly inert on every skill (≤.05 drops, facts/multilingual slightly improved). Mid-depth single blocks aren't good transferable units on this model. Late blocks (L30-L33) carry knowledge and language but leak into general_text.

[general] In a short run, run ablations in parallel batches of 2-3 before any screen. Every candidate this run failed at the ablate stage, so it cost no screens. Check the control column first: a control shift above about .1 rules out a screen even when the target drop is above .25.
